source_name: eForms SDK / eForms metadata reference (TED developer docs)
why_relevant: Since Feb 2024 all CZ above-threshold notices are eForms. The SDK defines field IDs, business terms and codelists — without it you cannot reliably extract buyer, lot, CPV, estimated value, winner and framework flags from CZ notices. Essential parsing dictionary for the whole A2 workstream.

source_name: TED Open Data Service (data.ted.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Bulk/linked-open-data face of TED. Enables retrospective full-history analysis of CZ banking and payment-services contracts (who won, at what value, how often re-tendered) instead of only forward monitoring. Best route for building the CZ baseline dataset.

source_name: TED CSV subset dataset on the EU Open Data Portal (data.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Flattened CSV of the key contract-notice and award fields — the fastest way to get a decade-scale CZ finance-CPV panel into a spreadsheet/DB without XML parsing. Coverage is a subset of fields, so it complements rather than replaces the API.

source_name: TED — European public procurement: principles & legal bases (SIMAP successor pages)
why_relevant: The old SIMAP content now lives under ted.europa.eu/simap. Gives the directive thresholds, form types and publication obligations that determine WHICH Czech banking/payment contracts must appear at EU level — i.e. it defines the boundary of what this cell can and cannot see.

source_name: CPV nomenclature (Common Procurement Vocabulary) — finance & payments branch 66/72
why_relevant: The classification keys that make TED monitoring precise for this sector: 66110000 banking services, 66113000 credit granting, 66172000 financial transaction processing and clearing-house services, plus 66600000 treasury and 72xxxxxx IT codes used for card/ATM/core-banking systems. Building the exact CPV pick-list is the single highest-leverage step for CZ coverage.

source_name: Opentender.eu — Czech Republic portal (Government Transparency Institute / DIGIWHIST)
why_relevant: Cleaned, entity-resolved merge of TED and the Czech national portal, with buyer and supplier profile pages and integrity/competition indicators. Useful for supplier-side questions ('which vendors keep winning CZ payment contracts') that raw TED makes laborious, and for spotting single-bidder or repeat-award patterns.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership Data Registry — Europe / TED (OpenTender) publication record
why_relevant: Registry entry documenting how TED data is republished in OCDS, its coverage and known quality caveats. Good for deciding whether to consume TED directly or via an OCDS mirror, and for finding further CZ-specific OCDS publishers.

source_name: DotaceEU.cz — Seznam operací (příjemců), EU cohesion funds 2021–2027
why_relevant: Mandatory EU transparency list of every EU-funded CZ operation and beneficiary, refreshed monthly. Where an EU-funded project involves payment infrastructure, digitalisation of municipal/state payment collection or banking services, this reveals the buyer and budget BEFORE or ALONGSIDE the TED notice — an early-warning layer on the EU-funds side of the cell.

source_name: Národní plán obnovy — planobnovy.gov.cz (RRF implementation, plnění NPO)
why_relevant: Czech Recovery and Resilience Facility programme site. RRF-funded digitalisation components (eGovernment, state payment/collection systems) generate above-threshold contracts that land in TED; the NPO milestone reporting tells you which components are funded and when procurement is due, giving a forward calendar for the cell.

source_name: MMR — Národní plán obnovy: Pravidla pro žadatele a příjemce (procurement rules for RRF beneficiaries)
why_relevant: Defines what RRF beneficiaries must do when awarding contracts, including the Art. 22(2)(d) data-collection duty on contractors/subcontractors and beneficial owners. Tells you what contract-level data legally exists for RRF-funded CZ procurements — the basis for FOI (zákon 106/1999) requests when TED alone is thin.

source_name: Ministry of the Interior — Národní plán obnovy: Veřejné zakázky page
why_relevant: A concrete worked example of a CZ ministry publishing its RRF-funded contracts in a dedicated NPO section — MV ČR is a major buyer of eGovernment and identity/payment-adjacent systems. Pattern-generalises: other ministries maintain equivalent NPO procurement sections worth enumerating.

source_name: SZIF — Seznam příjemců dotací z fondů EU (agricultural/EAFRD payment agency beneficiary register)
why_relevant: SZIF is itself a large CZ paying agency and a buyer of banking/payment-processing and card-disbursement services; it also publishes the mandatory EU beneficiary list. Dual value: a named CZ contracting authority to watch in TED, and an EU-transparency register in its own right.

source_name: MPO — Přehled příjemců dotací ze státního rozpočtu a evropských fondů
why_relevant: Ministry of Industry and Trade's §5(3) FOI publication of state and EU grant recipients. Demonstrates the CZ FOI-driven publication layer that sits under EU-funded procurement — a fallback route to contract-level detail when TED award notices omit values or suppress supplier names.

source_name: TED reusers workshop materials (Publications Office) — retrieving eForms
why_relevant: Publications Office guidance aimed precisely at organisations building TED monitoring pipelines: what changed with eForms, which retrieval routes remain, known pitfalls. Short-cuts a lot of trial and error when standing up the CZ feed.

source_name: Commercial TED mirrors / tender alert services (TenderWolf, Tenderlake, Tendersontime, jorpex, tedapi.pro)
why_relevant: Commercial resellers of TED content. Low evidentiary value (derivative, paywalled, unclear freshness) but useful in two ways: their public notice pages are sometimes indexed by search engines when the TED page is not, and their knowledge-base articles explain publication mechanics clearly. Treat as lead-generation, never as citation of record.

source_name: ÚOHS – Sborníky rozhodnutí (sectoral decision digests)
why_relevant: Curated sector digests of ÚOHS procurement decisions (e.g. healthcare 01/2021–06/2024, telecommunications/telematics 01/2021–12/2023). A banking/IT-flavoured digest, or the telecom/IT one, gives pre-filtered, thematically grouped case law — a shortcut into where the disputed tech tenders are.

source_name: ÚOHS – Tiskové zprávy: veřejné zakázky
why_relevant: Press releases flag the decisions ÚOHS itself considers significant, often weeks before the full text appears in the collection. Precedent: the joint ÚOHS–MMR position on concluding banking-service contracts after Sberbank CZ's collapse left public authorities without a bank — a direct market-opening signal for banking tenders.

source_name: ÚOHS – Návrh na přezkoumání úkonů zadavatele (procedural pages)
why_relevant: Explains the complaint pipeline (námitky → návrh → rozhodnutí → rozklad → správní soud), which defines the terminology, deposit rules and time windows a collector must model to know when a contested banking tender becomes visible and how long it stalls.

source_name: Hlídač státu – Databáze rozhodnutí ÚOHS
why_relevant: Independent NGO mirror of ÚOHS decisions in a structured, queryable dataset, cross-linked to Hlídač's contract register, company and tender datasets. Far easier to bulk-query than the ÚOHS site, and it joins a decision to the actual signed contract and supplier.

source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách (MMR) – Databáze rozhodnutí / Vybraná rozhodnutí od 2020
why_relevant: The ministry's own monthly 'Vybraná rozhodnutí ÚOHS' PDFs summarise the decisions the state considers precedent-setting, including administrative-court reviews. A compact monthly feed that tells you which contested tenders mattered without reading thousands of rulings.

source_name: Nejvyšší správní soud – vyhledávač rozhodnutí
why_relevant: Judicial review layer above ÚOHS: when a bank or IT vendor loses at ÚOHS it appeals to Krajský soud v Brně and then NSS. These judgments reveal the final outcome, the commercial stakes, and often more factual detail about the tender than the regulator's own text.

source_name: NKÚ – kontrolní závěry (audit conclusions)
why_relevant: Supreme Audit Office conclusions are public and unappealable, and routinely dissect payment-agenda and IT projects: e.g. KA 17/22 on MPSV benefit-payment agenda and system-integration services (explicitly assessing ZZVZ compliance), KA 16/30 on state treasury liquidity, KA 14/20 on the National Data Centre. They expose vendor lock-in, cost overruns and mismanaged banking/payment procurement in detail no tender notice contains.

source_name: Věstník NKÚ
why_relevant: The NKÚ bulletin carries the annual audit plan (which upcoming audits are scheduled) plus the published conclusions. The plan is forward-looking: knowing an audit of a payment or treasury system is scheduled predicts where remediation procurement will follow.

source_name: NKÚ – informace z kontrolních akcí (press summaries)
why_relevant: Short 'informace z kontrolní akce' summaries are published alongside the full conclusions and are the fastest low-cost trigger for deciding whether to pull the full PDF.

source_name: ČNB – Seznamy a evidence (lists and registers of regulated entities)
why_relevant: Authoritative entry point to every CZ licensed bank, payment institution, e-money institution, small-scale payment service provider and account information service provider. New licences identify the payment actors likely to bid for public banking/acquiring contracts or to be acquired; withdrawn licences explain sudden tender re-runs (cf. Sberbank).

source_name: ČNB JERRS – Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů (+ WS JERRS web services)
why_relevant: The machine-queryable licence register: search by name or IČO, with the full status history — licence granted, amended, withdrawn, with dates. This is the cleanest structured feed for detecting new payment actors and licence changes, and WS JERRS web services have exposed selected data since 1 July 2019.
